messages:
Nina (Docs): quick sync — I opened PR #1502 to tidy the reserved-pools quickstart, add a tiny CLI example, and tighten SLA language. Can folks verify accuracy before I merge? https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1502 :wave:
Omar (CLI): I can check CLI bits. Last week we changed flags to kebab-case for consistency. Use --eviction-priority and --isolation-level (values: low|medium|high and tenant|node|gpu).
Rhea (Runtime): a couple of runtime notes: we standardized on 'eviction' (not preemption). eviction_policy accepts graceful, immediate, delayed. delayed triggers a cooldown window (default 300s). eviction_priority is low|medium|high (lower = evict later).
Nina (Docs): thanks — current CLI snippet in PR is:
```bash
redwoodctl dedicated create-pool \
  --name "gpu-large" \
  --min-instances 2 \
  --max-instances 10 \
  --eviction-priority low \
  --isolation-level node
```
Omar (CLI): looks good. please ensure the flags are dashed in the docs and the example uses the exact flag names; tests pick that up.
Tom (Product): on SLA wording, avoid percentages in quickstart. Suggest: "Reserved capacity: baseline performance guaranteed per contract. Burst capacity: best-effort; subject to pool and regional availability." Link to the SLA reference for exact numbers.
Nina (Docs): I'll use Tom's phrasing and link to /handbook/enterprise/slas/dedicated.md. redwood-docs-bot: link check -> `/handbook/enterprise/slas/dedicated.md` exists.
Rhea (Runtime): also add a clear note that fallback routing to hosted API is controlled by routing_policy and tenant opt-in. Not automatic. Maybe a one-line callout on the flowchart: "Fallback to hosted only after sustained SLO violation per routing policy; Private customers can opt out."
Nina (Docs): adding that. Also adding two tiny YAML examples (graceful vs immediate) so readers see behavior differences. Draft YAML:
```yaml
# graceful (preferred)
name: gpu-large
min_instances: 2
max_instances: 10
eviction_policy: graceful
eviction_priority: low
isolation_level: node

# immediate (evict as soon as needed)
name: gpu-fast-evict
min_instances: 1
max_instances: 5
eviction_policy: immediate
eviction_priority: high
isolation_level: tenant
```
Omar (CLI): small nit: in the immediate example, maybe use eviction_priority: medium to show variety. High implies high likelihood of eviction, which is fine but examples should show realistic mixes.
Nina (Docs): ok switching to medium. Also adding parenthetical for delayed: `(cooldown default: 300s, configurable)`.
Tom (Product): add a short billing blurb: "Burst usage billed at on-demand rates; reserved pools billed under commitment." Link to pricing. Keep it one sentence.
redwood-docs-bot: CI check – found broken link in docs/quickstarts/dedicated.md -> recommended target `/handbook/dedicated/reserved-pools-guide.md`.
Nina (Docs): thanks bot — updating links to the guide path.
Rhea (Runtime): accessibility note: add alt text for the flowchart and a text-summary for screen readers. Small change but important.
Nina (Docs): will add alt text + short text summary.
Omar (CLI): once you push updates, ping me and I'll run the CLI examples through the smoke tests.
Tom (Product): I'll sanity-check the SLA/billing sentence. If legal wants changes we'll iterate in a follow-up PR.
Nina (Docs): great, I'll push fixes now (flags, YAML tweak, billing blurb, fallback callout, alt text, links). Please leave a single quick review if you can so we can merge today. Thanks!
